title: Evaluating a Fine-Tuned Agent
summary: Work through Evaluating a Fine-Tuned Agent.

blocks.md: This lesson follows **Evaluating a Fine-Tuned Agent** in *Trajectory Fine-Tuning* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Trajectory Fine-Tuning, § Evaluating a Fine-Tuned Agent
blocks.md: A fine-tuned checkpoint can reach a low loss on a repair corpus yet fail to resolve actual connection-pool leaks in production. Training configurations and data manifests record how an artifact was produced, but only closed-loop trials reveal how the policy navigates multi-step execution when its own actions dictate future observations. The task acceptance contract defined in a later section governs these trials, addressing the specific failure modes and behavioral shifts that weight updates introduce.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Schema augmentation matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A corpus with one static tool signature lets the policy memorize argument keys, so augmentation transforms the whole decision context coherently and robustness is measured on held-out schemas.

questions.q: The section **Evaluating a Fine-Tuned Agent** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A corpus with one static tool signature lets the policy memorize argument keys, so augmentation transforms the whole decision context coherently and robustness is measured on held-out schemas.
Loss values are comparable only under identical split, serialization, mask, and normalization, and promotion requires closed-loop task acceptance under the serving configuration, not lower loss.
Fine-tuning changes only the proposal distribution, so stable procedure can move into weights, deployment-varying contracts stay in context, and enforcement stays in the runtime.

When several admissible continuations succeed but differ in cost or risk, DPO over selected spans raises the preferred record's reference-relative score against the dispreferred one from an identical context.

terms.def: A policy is assessed on the task outcomes produced by its own actions under a fixed contract and budget, independently of teacher-forced loss.
